idiom_name: filtered()/where() returning a criterion-taking filterer + first-class predicates (and/or/not)
implementation_notes: Language-neutral form: give the container one entry point that returns a filterer bound to it - either a function value or a small functional interface whose single operation takes a criterion and returns a filtered copy of the container's own type (filtered(), where(keep), filter(predicate)). The criterion is the caller's value: a function, closure, function pointer with context, function object or predicate interface over the element type or a supertype of it. Implement the copy by selecting the survivors and constructing a new instance of the container's own type with the same identity and metadata. Instead of a second method per criterion, let callers compose criteria (and/or/not, guards) and pass them in; where the language supports it, make the filterer generic (Filterer<G, E>) and use use-site variance (? extends G, ? super E) so subtypes are supported without additional methods.
code_sketch:
container.filtered().by(keep)      # or container.filtered(keep)
#   filtered() -> a filterer bound to this container
#   by(keep)   -> new container of the same type, only elements where keep(e)

keep  = namedCriterion1.and(namedCriterion2)   # criteria are values and compose
small = container.filtered(keep)               # identity and metadata preserved
pitfalls: Returning a bare element list (or a live view of the internal storage) instead of a container-typed copy: the first loses the container's meaning, the second lets later writes to the source appear inside the 'filtered' result.
Criteria that are not functions of the element alone - stateful predicates, lazy loads, clock or configuration reads - answer differently on the second evaluation.
Growing the API with one method per criterion (or one per subtype narrowing) instead of letting callers pass criteria: that duplication is exactly what the pattern removes.

Wrong move: naming a servlet-style request middleware chain a 'filterer' -> callers expect Intercepting Filter semantics (FilterChain ordering, pre/post around a target) and the two patterns get conflated -> instead reserve Filterer for element selection that returns a same-typed copy and call request interception middleware.

Wrong move: keeping an in-memory predicate and a hand-written query translation of the same criterion side by side -> the two drift and tests that exercise only the predicate pass while the executed query diverges -> instead derive the query from one inspectable criterion (expression trees, JPA Criteria) or run the same fixtures through both paths.

Wrong move: introducing a filterer type per entity for a small, fixed set of criteria -> the extra types and indirection cost more than the findByX methods they replaced -> instead stay with plain lambdas or the native filter and introduce the filterer only once criteria get named, composed or passed across layers.
